> **Draft.** The mechanism is measured and bit-exact, but coverage is three call
> sites out of the ~1191 small launches a Z-Image step makes. Opening it early
> for a read on the approach and on where the crate belongs.

## Motivation

At low resolution a diffusion step is not a few large kernels, it is a long tail of small ones. Profiling Z-Image-Turbo at 512x512, 4 steps on one H200:

| | |
|---|---|
| kernels | 2108 |
| mean kernel | **26.6 us** |
| GPU busy | 36.9% |
| **GPU idle** | **63.1%** |
| idle behind each kernel | **45.5 us** |

76% of those kernels run under 20 us and together account for 15% of the busy time. The device is finished long before Python and the Triton launcher can describe the next launch.

This is regime-specific, and the regime is set by kernel size rather than by parallelism. The same engine on MiniMax-H3 at 768p across 8 GPUs, Ulysses8, eager, idles **0.3%** — kernels there average 482.8 us. Sharding the sequence does not change that: it divides the work per kernel's *sequence*, not the kernel's absolute size.

## Modifications

`rust/sglang-launch`, a PyO3 extension holding `LaunchChain`: record a launch as (function, grid, block, arguments), then replay it through `cuLaunchKernel`. Kept out of the root workspace exactly as `sglang-radix-tree` is, and for the
same reason — PyO3 0.22 cannot share a dependency graph with the workspace's native `links = "python"` crates.

Python side, `fast_launch.CachedLaunch` keys recordings by signature (shape, stride, dtype, eps — not addresses). First call of a signature runs the ordinary Triton path and records; later calls rebind pointers and replay.

Three entry points adopt it: `rmsnorm_scale`, `rmsnorm_tanh_residual`, `zimage_qk_rmsnorm_native`. No model definition changes.

Unlike the breakable-graph path a recording survives a shape change: a new signature records a new entry rather than forcing a recapture. That matters for models whose sequence length depends on the prompt — MiniMax-H3 stays eager in its validated deployment precisely because prompt-dependent packed boundaries miss a captured signature.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-exact, which is the point: the same kernel runs with the same grid and
arguments in the same order, so only host latency changes.

- Call site: `torch.equal(triton_result, replayed_result)` is True, max abs
  difference 0.
- End to end: same prompt and seed generated with the extension importable and
  not, PNG sha256 identical (`34aab947d442b26c3cf8c793728f21e5...`).

This is what `torch.compile` cannot offer here — it is a measured comparator on
this codebase, not a lossless baseline.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Z-Image-Turbo, 1x H200, 512x512, 4 steps, eager, no compile, no breakable graph:

| entry points hooked | window | GPU idle | per step |
|---|---|---|---|
| none (baseline) | 167.31 ms | 63.1% | 131.3 ms |
| 1 | 163.76 ms | 62.2% | 127.2 ms |
| **3** | **129.74 ms** | **51.6%** | **107.7 ms** |

**1.29x end to end, step -18.0%, idle 63.1% -> 51.6%.**

Two results worth recording separately.

**The cut has to be deeper than the launcher.** At a single call site,
replacing only the Triton launcher was worth 1.36x (27.15 -> 19.93 us).
Short-circuiting sglang's own per-call validation and stride derivation as well
took it to 2.33x (27.27 -> 11.73 us). Half the cost was bookkeeping *around*
the launch, not the launch.

**Gain tracks coverage, linearly.** One entry point moved the step 2.1%; three
moved it 18%. The remaining ~890 small launches per step are ATen elementwise
rather than Triton and need a different hook.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — none yet; draft
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — none yet; draft
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Open questions for review

1. **Build integration.** The crate is registered in `extension-manifests` but
   nothing builds or ships it yet; `fast_launch.available()` returns False and
   every call takes the existing path. How should it be wired — alongside
   `sglang-radix-tree`, or behind an extra?
2. **Coverage.** Worth extending to the ATen elementwise launches, or is a
   Triton-only hook the right boundary?
3. **Signature cache growth.** One entry per (shape, stride, dtype, eps). Fine
   for fixed-resolution serving; a bound may be wanted for arbitrary shapes.

nodes.body:
Pushed two commits so this builds and actually takes effect:

- `fcd9c8c8`: edition 2024 needs `unsafe extern "C"` for the libcuda block (rustc 1.98 rejects the bare one). `fast_launch` also imported `sgl_launch` from the top level, but `setup.py` installs the crate at its `python-module` path (`sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.norm.sgl_launch`), so the Rust path was silently off. It now imports from that path.
- `13cf5569`: merged `main` (conflict in `rust/Cargo.toml`: kept main's members and added `sglang-launch` to `exclude` and `extension-manifests`).

Measured on GB300 (aarch64, rustc 1.98.1): `cargo build --release` succeeds and `fast_launch._HAVE_RUST_LAUNCH` is `True` with the cdylib at that path. Z-Image-Turbo 1024², TP2, eager, served on 2xGB300 with NUMA-bound workers (#43565). Median of 5 after 2 warmups, fresh server per arm, 2 interleaved rounds:

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main + fixes | 0.522 s | 0.518 s |
| + this PR | **0.471 s** | **0.463 s** |

That is about 10% faster, consistent in both rounds. An earlier run without NUMA binding was too noisy to read.

@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Rust-backed launch path for hot Triton kernels.
+
+At low resolution a diffusion step is a long tail of small kernels: Z-Image-Turbo
+at 512x512 runs 2108 kernels averaging 26.6 us with 45.5 us of GPU idle behind
+each one. The device is not the constraint there. Python and the Triton launcher
+are, and describing a launch costs more than performing it.
+
+Neither the kernel nor its argument layout changes between steps, only the
+buffers do. So record one launch per signature, then rebind the pointers and
+replay through ``cuLaunchKernel`` from Rust. Same kernel, same grid, same
+arguments, same order, so results are bit-identical: this removes host latency
+and nothing else.
+
+Unlike a CUDA graph it survives a shape change -- a new signature records a new
+entry rather than forcing a recapture of everything -- which matters for models
+whose sequence length depends on the prompt.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import torch
+
+try:
+    # setup.py installs the crate at its declared python-module path.
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.norm import sgl_launch
+
+    _HAVE_RUST_LAUNCH = True
+except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - extension not built
+    sgl_launch = None
+    _HAVE_RUST_LAUNCH = False
+
+
+def available() -> bool:
+    return _HAVE_RUST_LAUNCH
+
+
+class CachedLaunch:
+    """One Triton kernel's launches, keyed by signature.
+
+    ``record`` is called on the first sighting of a signature, after the
+    ordinary Triton path has produced the result and the ``CompiledKernel``.
+    ``lookup`` plus ``replay`` is the steady state and touches no dispatcher.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._chains: dict[tuple, object] = {}
+
+    def lookup(self, signature: tuple):
+        return self._chains.get(signature)
+
+    def record(
+        self,
+        signature: tuple,
+        compiled,
+        grid: tuple[int, int, int],
+        pointer_args: list[int],
+        scalar_args: list[int],
+    ) -> None:
+        if not _HAVE_RUST_LAUNCH or signature in self._chains:
+            return
+        chain = sgl_launch.LaunchChain()
+        threads = compiled.metadata.num_warps * compiled.metadata.warp_size
+        # Triton appends scratch pointers to every kernel's parameter list. They
+        # are null when unused, but the slots exist and the driver rejects a
+        # short argument array.
+        scratch = [0, 0]
+        chain.record(
+            compiled.function,
+            grid,
+            (threads, 1, 1),
+            compiled.metadata.shared,
+            list(pointer_args) + list(scalar_args) + scratch,
+        )
+        self._chains[signature] = chain
+
+    def replay(self, chain, pointer_args: list[int]) -> None:
+        for index, value in enumerate(pointer_args):
+            chain.rebind(0, index, value)
+        chain.replay(torch.cuda.current_stream().cuda_stream)

+import struct
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.norm import fast_launch as _fast_launch
+
+_RMSNORM_SCALE_LAUNCH = _fast_launch.CachedLaunch()
+_RMSNORM_TANH_LAUNCH = _fast_launch.CachedLaunch()
+
+
+def _f32_bits(value: float) -> int:
+    """An fp32 kernel argument as the 4 bytes the driver will read."""
+    return struct.unpack("<I", struct.pack("<f", float(value)))[0]
+
+
+def _scale_signature(x, weight, scale, eps):
+    """What a recorded rmsnorm_scale launch stays valid for.
+
+    Strides belong in the key because the kernel indexes rows with them, and
+    dtype because the compiled kernel is specialized on it. Buffer addresses do
+    not: those are rebound per call, which is the whole point.
+    """
+    return (
+        x.shape,
+        x.stride(),
+        x.dtype,
+        weight.shape,
+        scale.shape,
+        scale.stride(),
+        eps,
+    )
+
+
+def _tanh_signature(x, gate, residual, weight, eps):
+    """What a recorded gated-residual launch stays valid for."""
+    return (
+        x.shape,
+        x.stride(),
+        x.dtype,
+        gate.shape,
+        gate.stride(),
+        residual.stride(),
+        weight.shape,
+        eps,
+    )
+
+

     x: torch.Tensor,
     weight: torch.Tensor,
     scale: torch.Tensor,
     eps: float,
 ) -> torch.Tensor | None:
     """Apply BF16-native ``RMSNorm(x) * scale`` or return ``None``."""
+    # Operand validation, stride derivation and the power-of-two block below
+    # are decided by the signature, never by the values. At this kernel's size
+    # that bookkeeping costs more than the launch it guards, so a signature
+    # seen before goes straight to rebinding pointers and replaying.
+    if _fast_launch.available():
+        cached = _RMSNORM_SCALE_LAUNCH.lookup(_scale_signature(x, weight, scale, eps))
+        if cached is not None:
+            out = torch.empty_like(x, memory_format=torch.contiguous_format)
+            _RMSNORM_SCALE_LAUNCH.replay(
+                cached,
+                [
+                    out.data_ptr(),
+                    x.data_ptr(),
+                    weight.data_ptr(),
+                    scale.data_ptr(),
+                ],
+            )
+            return out
+
     if not _can_use_operand(x, weight, scale):
         return None

+version = "0.1.0"
+edition = "2024"
+description = "Replayable CUDA kernel launches for launch-bound diffusion steps"
+license = "Apache-2.0"
+repository = "https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang"
+
+[package.metadata.sglang]
+python-module = "sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.norm.sgl_launch"
+debug = false
+
+[lib]
+name = "sgl_launch"
+crate-type = ["cdylib"]
+
+# Kept out of the root workspace for the same reason as sglang-radix-tree: this
+# crate is on PyO3 0.22, which cannot share a dependency graph with the
+# workspace's native `links = "python"` crates.
+[workspace]
+
+[dependencies]
+pyo3 = { version = "0.22", features = ["extension-module"] }
+
+[profile.release]
+opt-level = 3
+lto = true
+codegen-units = 1
+panic = "abort"

issue_comments.body:
Pushed two commits so this builds and actually takes effect:

- `fcd9c8c8`: edition 2024 needs `unsafe extern "C"` for the libcuda block (rustc 1.98 rejects the bare one). `fast_launch` also imported `sgl_launch` from the top level, but `setup.py` installs the crate at its `python-module` path (`sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.norm.sgl_launch`), so the Rust path was silently off. It now imports from that path.
- `13cf5569`: merged `main` (conflict in `rust/Cargo.toml`: kept main's members and added `sglang-launch` to `exclude` and `extension-manifests`).

Measured on GB300 (aarch64, rustc 1.98.1): `cargo build --release` succeeds and `fast_launch._HAVE_RUST_LAUNCH` is `True` with the cdylib at that path. Z-Image-Turbo 1024², TP2, eager, served on 2xGB300 with NUMA-bound workers (#43565). Median of 5 after 2 warmups, fresh server per arm, 2 interleaved rounds:

| | round 1 | round 2 |
|---|---|---|
| main + fixes | 0.522 s | 0.518 s |
| + this PR | **0.471 s** | **0.463 s** |

That is about 10% faster, consistent in both rounds. An earlier run without NUMA binding was too noisy to read.
